about: Every function a template expression may call, for both engines: cel-expr-python on the server and cel-js in the browser. 'where' says who provides an overload: 'skjald' (Skjald implements it on both sides), 'engine' (both engines have it built in) or 'browser' (the server's engine has it, Skjald adds it in the browser). The validator refuses any other function. Each side has a test holding its own declarations to this file, and the examples run on both engines with the cases in cases.json.

banned.matches: matches() isn't allowed in templates: use re_match(), which uses the same safe regular expressions on the server and in the browser.

functions.name: xor
functions.summary: True when exactly one of the two is true.

functions.name: switch
functions.summary: The value for the first argument from a map of cases, or the last argument when no case matches.

functions.name: re_match
functions.summary: Whether the text contains a match for the regular expression (RE2 syntax).

functions.name: re_replace
functions.summary: Replaces every match of the regular expression (RE2 syntax). In the replacement, $1 or ${name} is a captured group and $$ is a dollar sign.

functions.name: replace
functions.summary: Replaces every occurrence of some text with other text.

functions.name: size
functions.summary: The number of characters in text, or of items in a list or map.

functions.name: contains
functions.summary: Whether the text contains other text.

functions.name: startsWith
functions.summary: Whether the text starts with other text.

functions.name: endsWith
functions.summary: Whether the text ends with other text.

functions.name: upperAscii
functions.summary: The text in capitals (the letters A to Z only).

functions.name: lowerAscii
functions.summary: The text in small letters (the letters A to Z only).

functions.name: trim
functions.summary: The text without spaces at either end.

functions.name: split
functions.summary: The pieces of the text between each separator.

functions.name: join
functions.summary: The items of a list of text, with a separator between them.

functions.name: substring
functions.summary: Part of the text, from one position up to (not including) another, counting from 0.

functions.name: indexOf
functions.summary: Where other text first appears in the text, counting from 0, or -1 when it doesn't.

functions.name: int
functions.summary: A whole number from text or a decimal (decimals are cut, not rounded).

functions.name: double
functions.summary: A decimal number from text or a whole number.

functions.name: string
functions.summary: A value as text.

functions.name: format_number
functions.summary: A number as text with a set number of decimals, written the way the report's language writes numbers (1.234,5 in Danish, 1,234.5 in English). Halves round away from zero.

functions.name: sum
functions.summary: The total of a list of numbers: a whole number if every item is one, otherwise a decimal.

functions.name: has
functions.summary: Whether a row of a repeating group has a value for a column.

functions.name: exists
functions.summary: Whether any item in a list meets a condition.

functions.name: all
functions.summary: Whether every item in a list meets a condition.

functions.name: exists_one
functions.summary: Whether exactly one item in a list meets a condition.

functions.name: filter
functions.summary: The items in a list that meet a condition; .size() counts them.

functions.name: map
functions.summary: A new list with something worked out for each item, such as one column of a repeating group.

functions.name: lookup
functions.summary: A value from one of the shared library's data tables: the first value column, or the named one. Empty when the table or key doesn't exist.

functions.name: timestamp
functions.summary: A point in time from text in RFC 3339 form, such as 2026-10-21T03:20:00Z. For a local date and time, use date().

functions.name: duration
functions.summary: A length of time, such as "72h" or "90m", to add to or subtract from a point in time.

functions.name: date
functions.summary: A point in time from a date (2026-10-21) or a date and time (2026-10-21T14:30), read in the company's time zone unless it names one.

functions.name: add_hours
functions.summary: A point in time a number of hours later (or earlier, for a negative number).

functions.name: add_days
functions.summary: The same time of day a number of calendar days later (or earlier), in the company's time zone.

functions.name: hours_between
functions.summary: The hours from the first point in time to the second, as a decimal; negative if the second comes first.

functions.name: days_between
functions.summary: The calendar days from the first date to the second, in the company's time zone; negative if the second comes first.

functions.name: format_date
functions.summary: A point in time as text in the company's time zone and the report's language. yyyy year, MMMM month name, MMM short month name, MM month (01–12), M month, dd day (01–31), d day, EEEE weekday, HH hour (00–23), mm minutes, ss seconds; text in 'single quotes' is kept as written.
